newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end near day's lows, off early 4,000.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end near day's lows, off early 4,000.

text.p: Share prices at Bombay bourses ended near the day's lowest levels on Monday, in a day of wild price swings as post-budget euphoria played on the minds of market operators, traders said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) finished with a net gain of 12.85 points, or 0.33 percent, erasing a sharp 150.42 points, or 3.9 percent rally in early morning trade.
"I guess there is a certain amount of profit-taking which is quite healthy. It doesn't look like there is a trend reversal," said Prashant Purker, head of sales at Peregrine Capital India Ltd.
The index rocketed to an eight-month high in morning deals, but traders said lack of follow-up buying by foreign funds and profit-taking by speculators erased the gains.
"This reaction is quite healthy. It only gives opportunity for more people to enter the market," said the head of dealing at a foreign securities firm who did not wish to be named.
The breadth and focus of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's 1997/98 (April-March) budget last Friday, boosted market confidence and sent investors on a buying spree, traders said.
"I expect the market to form a bottom in the next few days and break the all-time high of 4,643 reached in September 1995."
BHEL closed 14.25 rupees up at 405.0, Colgate 15.0 to 355.0 and Arvind Mills 7.50 to 156.0. Among pivotals, Reliance fell 4.50 rupees to 305.50, SBI 8.0 to 323.75.
"Foreign funds will go in for large market-capitalised stocks. Having missed the rally, they must be frustrated." Ajit Dayal, director at Quantum Financial Services, said.

"Anyone who doubted that reforms were on the stumbling block are now silent. The coalition has given us a fantastic budget," Quantum's Dayal said. He forecast the index would hit 4,500 points within three months.
